You are now performing a forensic verification of the Playa AI website implementation.

Your task is to produce a complete, evidence-based report that will be reviewed independently against the original “Playa AI — Website Audit (July 2026)” PDF.

IMPORTANT RULES

* Do not edit, format, refactor, generate, or delete any project files.
* Do not automatically fix problems.
* Do not publish or deploy.
* Do not rely only on `verify:audit`, `check:copy`, or previous reports.
* Inspect the actual current source code and built output.
* Distinguish clearly between:

  * verified in source;
  * verified in production build;
  * verified manually in the browser;
  * reported by a script only;
  * blocked or requiring a human decision;
  * not verified.
* Never mark an item complete without showing evidence.
* If the original audit PDF is unavailable in the workspace, state that clearly. Do not pretend that `BLOCKERS.md` is the original audit.
* Preserve the original PDF’s item numbering. Do not replace audit items 26–36 with newer implementation tasks.
* Do not hide failed checks, warnings, unresolved decisions, soft-404 behavior, or platform limitations.

## 1. Establish repository state

Run and report the complete output of:

```bash
pwd
git status --short
git branch --show-current
git log -1 --oneline
git diff --stat
git diff --name-only
git diff --check
```

Also report:

* package manager and version;
* Node.js version;
* application framework;
* build tool;
* current canonical source directory;
* whether uncommitted files exist;
* every file changed by the website remediation.

Do not expose secrets, tokens, credentials, or `.env` values.

## 2. Locate the audit evidence

Check for the following:

```bash
rg --files | rg -i 'audit|blockers|report|pdf|llms|robots|sitemap'
```

Report which of these are present:

* Original Playa AI audit PDF
* `BLOCKERS.md`
* `public/llms.txt`
* `public/robots.txt`
* sitemap
* copy-check script
* audit-verification script

If the original PDF is present, use it as the primary audit source. If it is absent, say:

> Original audit PDF unavailable in this workspace. The following is a code-evidence report, not an independent PDF-to-code comparison.

## 3. Execute all validation commands

Run every applicable command and include:

* exact command;
* exit code;
* complete success/failure summary;
* number of checks;
* warnings;
* skipped checks;
* failure details.

Required commands:

```bash
pnpm run check:copy
pnpm run typecheck
pnpm run build
pnpm run verify:audit
```

Then inspect `package.json` and run these only if the scripts exist:

```bash
pnpm run lint
pnpm run test
```

If a script does not exist, report `NOT AVAILABLE`. Do not claim it passed.

Also report:

* number of routes prerendered;
* generated JS and CSS bundle names;
* build warnings;
* whether the working tree changed after running validation.

Run `git status --short` again at the end.

## 4. Validate the validators

Inspect:

* `scripts/check-copy.js`
* `scripts/verify-audit.js`
* relevant `package.json` scripts

Explain:

* exactly which files and routes each script scans;
* prohibited strings checked;
* structural assertions checked;
* important audit requirements not covered;
* whether a check could pass despite a visible or runtime problem;
* whether Classic/archive pages are intentionally excluded;
* whether the reported `83/83` represents 83 independent audit requirements or 83 implementation assertions.

Do not treat the scripts as proof of requirements they do not test.

## 5. Original PDF audit matrix

Create a table preserving all original audit items and original numbering:

| Audit ID | Original finding/title | Priority | Required action | Current status | Source evidence | Build/browser evidence | Remaining work |
| -------- | ---------------------- | -------: | --------------- | -------------- | --------------- | ---------------------- | -------------- |

Allowed statuses:

* `VERIFIED FIXED`
* `PARTIALLY FIXED`
* `NOT FIXED`
* `BLOCKED`
* `NEEDS HUMAN DECISION`
* `NOT APPLICABLE`
* `NOT VERIFIED`

Requirements:

* Include every original numbered audit item.
* Do not renumber or substitute newer tasks.
* For fixed items, provide exact file paths and current line ranges.
* Include a maximum three-line source excerpt when useful.
* For blocked items, explain the blocker precisely.
* If the PDF is unavailable, do not invent original titles. Instead, produce a separate “known requirements matrix” and label it incomplete.

## 6. Verify the comprehensive implementation items

Verify each implementation item separately:

* A — Organizational wording
* B — Three homepage initiatives only
* C — Workstreams card
* D — Work page content order
* E — Manifesto disclosure
* F — Website content review date
* G — `llms.txt`
* H — Image accessibility
* I — Link and keyboard accessibility
* J — Pledge modal wording and behavior
* K — `check:copy`
* L — `verify:audit`
* `BLOCKERS.md`

Use this table:

| Item | Claimed change | Source proof | Build proof | Browser proof | Status | Problems found |
| ---- | -------------- | ------------ | ----------- | ------------- | ------ | -------------- |

Do not skip Item I merely because no files were changed.

## 7. Perform the missing Item I accessibility sweep

Inspect every canonical page, shared navigation, footer, mobile menu, buttons, forms, dialogs, and internal links.

Report results for:

### Links and controls

* broken internal links;
* empty `href`;
* placeholder `href="#"`;
* links pointing to removed routes or missing anchors;
* buttons incorrectly implemented as links or vice versa;
* external links opening new tabs;
* accessible names for icon-only controls;
* duplicate interactive controls;
* controls unreachable by keyboard.

### Keyboard behavior

Test, where supported:

* logical Tab and Shift+Tab order;
* visible keyboard focus;
* skip-link behavior;
* navigation and mobile-menu operation;
* Enter and Space activation;
* Escape closing menus and modals;
* modal focus trapping;
* initial focus when a modal opens;
* focus returning to the triggering control when it closes;
* no keyboard traps.

### Structure and semantics

Inspect:

* one meaningful H1 per page;
* logical heading hierarchy;
* main/nav/footer landmarks;
* form labels;
* validation/error messaging;
* image alt text;
* decorative images using empty alt text correctly;
* ARIA attributes matching actual behavior;
* color-only communication;
* reduced-motion handling where applicable.

For every failure, provide:

* route;
* component;
* file and line;
* reproduction steps;
* severity;
* suggested fix.

Do not implement the fixes.

## 8. Page-by-page route verification

List every canonical route and every Classic/archive route.

For every canonical route report:

| Route | Renders | Title | Description | Canonical | H1 | Footer review date | Broken links | Console errors | Status |
| ----- | ------- | ----- | ----------- | --------- | -- | ------------------ | ------------ | -------------- | ------ |

Specifically verify:

* homepage;
* Work;
* Team/About;
* Events;
* Manifesto;
* Get involved/pledge flow;
* Privacy route;
* unknown route/404 behavior;
* all routes included in sitemap and prerendering.

Report route-name differences rather than assuming the expected names.

## 9. Copy and organizational consistency

Search the complete canonical source for all old, prohibited, or potentially inconsistent wording.

At minimum search for:

```bash
rg -n -i \
  -e 'Built in the desert' \
  -e 'Published for everyone' \
  -e 'philanthropic initiative fiscally sponsored' \
  -e 'Agent Labs running monthly' \
  -e 'Human Connection Research' \
  -e 'sign the pledge' \
  -e 'sign it' \
  -e '501\\(c\\)\\(3\\)' \
  -e 'Mystic Arts Foundation' \
  -e 'Born on the Playa' \
  artifacts/playa-ai/src public scripts
```

Adjust the source path if the project uses a different location.

Report every occurrence and classify it as:

* correct canonical copy;
* intentional archive copy;
* metadata copy;
* prohibited stale copy;
* unrelated match.

Verify organizational wording across:

* visible page content;
* footer;
* Team/About;
* metadata;
* SSR/prerender route data;
* structured data;
* `llms.txt`;
* sitemap/SEO files where applicable.

## 10. Content and factual-claim verification

Report all claims involving:

* fiscal sponsorship;
* California nonprofit status;
* U.S. 501(c)(3) status;
* number of initiatives;
* number of workstreams;
* current programs versus intended exploration;
* event participation;
* grants or microgrants;
* metrics or measured outcomes;
* license status;
* privacy practices;
* Founding Adopter status;
* Burning Man participant distinction.

Classify each claim:

* supported by provided project evidence;
* softened/disclosed appropriately;
* inconsistent between pages;
* needs human/legal confirmation;
* potentially misleading.

Do not make legal conclusions. Flag claims requiring confirmation.

## 11. SEO and machine-readable files

Verify:

* unique page titles;
* meta descriptions;
* canonical URLs;
* Open Graph metadata;
* robots directives;
* sitemap routes;
* `llms.txt`;
* 404 `noindex`;
* structured data;
* archive-page indexing behavior;
* Gmail addresses or prohibited contact data;
* production-domain consistency.

Show mismatches between visible content, metadata, and machine-readable files.

## 12. BLOCKERS.md review

Compare `BLOCKERS.md` with the actual code.

Report:

* blockers that remain accurate;
* blockers already resolved but still listed;
* missing blockers;
* items incorrectly marked complete;
* anything requiring legal, organizational, hosting, privacy, or licensing decisions.

Important:

* Determine whether its “36-item compliance matrix” actually preserves the original PDF’s 36 items.
* If it does not, label that matrix a “Comprehensive Implementation Matrix.”
* Do not modify the file during this verification.

## 13. Hosting and production limitations

Separate local findings from production-only checks.

Create a post-deployment checklist for:

* actual HTTP status of an unknown route;
* `/privacy` response;
* canonical-domain redirects;
* compression;
* cache headers;
* security headers;
* robots and sitemap availability;
* `llms.txt` availability;
* Open Graph rendering;
* console/network errors.

For cache and compression tests, use an actual generated hashed JS or CSS asset—not only the `/assets/` directory.

If the site is not deployed in this session, mark these `POST-DEPLOYMENT REQUIRED`.

## 14. Final verdict

End with exactly these sections:

### Verified complete

List only requirements supported by direct evidence.

### Partially complete

List requirements with incomplete implementation or incomplete evidence.

### Not fixed

List confirmed outstanding issues.

### Blocked or decision-gated

List hosting, legal, privacy, license, factual, and organizational decisions.

### Verification coverage gaps

List anything your checks could not prove.

### Regression risks

List areas most likely to break after future edits.

### Publication recommendation

Choose exactly one:

* `READY TO PUBLISH`
* `READY TO PUBLISH WITH DOCUMENTED BLOCKERS`
* `NOT READY TO PUBLISH`

Explain the decision using evidence.

### Required next actions

Provide a prioritized checklist:

* P0 — must resolve before publication;
* P1 — should resolve before publication;
* P2 — post-publication or decision-gated.

## Required response quality

* Be precise and skeptical.
* Do not say “all fixed” merely because scripts pass.
* Do not omit failing results.
* Do not use vague statements such as “looks good.”
* Cite exact files and current line ranges.
* Clearly distinguish code inspection from runtime/browser testing.
* Preserve the original audit numbering.
* Include Item I.
* Return the entire report in your response.
* Make no source-code changes.
